hex: # What `parse` makes of a text given as bytes. `hex` is the bytes, two
# digits each; `expected` and `opts` are as a row of ../spec/ has them.
# Only the TypeScript package takes bytes yet (see ../AGENTS.md).
# Bytes are read by their byte order mark, and as UTF-8 without one. The
# text of the first six rows is one description, whose title is `é` and a
# character outside the basic plane: as UTF-8, as UTF-8 behind its mark,
# and as UTF-16 and UTF-32 in each byte order behind theirs.
# Bytes that are not well-formed in their encoding are read as U+FFFD, one
# for each byte that starts no character, and are refused under `strict`.
# In UTF-16: half of a surrogate pair alone, and a byte left over at the
# In UTF-32: a character past U+10FFFF.
# Well-formed bytes are strict JSON like any other text, behind a mark
# One mark is passed over, and a second is text: it starts a plain scalar,
# so the root is a string, or it is part of a member name. Strict JSON
# refuses it. In UTF-8, then in UTF-16.
# A text that is refused for its encoding is not handed to the grammar,
# whatever its opening is: two thousand quotation marks, the second of
# them a byte that starts no character.
